diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that a finite index set \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb{N}^{d}\) is downward-closed in one direction.

we say that an index set \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb{N}^{d}\) is \textit{downward-closed in one direction} if there is a coordinate index \(j\in\{1,\dots,d\}\) such that whenever \((1,\dots1,\ell,1\dots,1)\in\Lambda\) holds, where \(\ell\) is in the \(j\)-th position, then for all integers \(k\leq\ell\) we also have \((1,\dots1,k,1\dots,1)\in\Lambda\).

issues.failure_explanation: The definition is a conditional and is vacuously satisfied by sets that contain no axis points, e.g., \(\Lambda=\{(2,2)\}\) in \(d=2\). The proof requires an axis point to define \(\overline{\ell}_{1}\) and \(n\), so the construction of \(h_{\Lambda}\) and the reduction to the univariate lower bound are not justified for all sets satisfying the stated hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Without loss of generality, we assume that \(\Lambda\) is downward-closed in the first coordinate. Then, for some \(\overline{\ell}_{1}\in\mathbb{N}\) we have \((\ell_{1},1\dots,1)\in\Lambda\) for all \(\ell_{1}=1,\dots,\overline{\ell}_{1}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis that \(\Lambda\) contains at least one point of the form \((1,\dots,\ell,\dots,1)\) (or is nonempty and downward-closed in the usual componentwise sense) before defining \(\overline{\ell}_{1}\).
issues.overall_effect: The general lower bound is not established for the full class of index sets claimed; the proof only works for sets containing an axis point.
issues.title: Missing existence of an axis point in downward-closed-in-one-direction assumption
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local strengthening of the hypothesis; the main isotropic case and intended applications already satisfy it, and the substantive lower bound for those cases is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Since \(S_{\Lambda_L}\) is a linear combination of differences \(\Delta_\ell=Q_\ell-Q_{\ell-1}\), the tensor product Gauss rules that actually appear with nonzero coefficient are not indexed by \(\Lambda_L\). For example, for \(d=2\) and \(L=4\), the coefficient of \(Q_1\otimes Q_1\) is \(1-1-1+1=0\), so its nodes are not used. Thus \(N\) is not \(\sum_{\ell\in\Lambda_L}\prod n_{\ell_k}\). This invalidates the derivation of \(N\asymp M^L L^{d-1}\).

failure_location.quote: Given the choice \(\Lambda_{L}=\bigl\{\boldsymbol{\ell}=(\ell_{1},\dots,\ell_{d})\in\mathbb{N}^{d}:|\boldsymbol{\ell}|_{1}\le L\bigr\}\), and in view of the well-known representation formula of the Smolyak algorithm (see e.g.,~\cite[Lemma 15.1]{Novak.E_Wozniakowski_book_2}) the total number of point evaluation \(N\) can be written explicitly as \(N=\sum_{\boldsymbol{\ell}\in\Lambda_{L}}\prod_{k=1}^{d}n_{\ell_{k}}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect counting formula with the standard Smolyak representation (the set of multi-indices with \(L-d+1\le|\ell|_1\le L\)) and re-derive the asymptotic bounds \(N\asymp M^L L^{d-1}\).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the lower bound for the isotropic sparse-grid quadrature does not establish the required relation between \(N\) and \(n_{L-d+1}\); the theorem's lower bound is not rigorously proven as written.
issues.title: Incorrect formula for the number of point evaluations in Smolyak quadrature
issues.why_classification: The theorem's conclusion is likely still true, but the proof needs a contained nontrivial correction to the counting of point evaluations and the subsequent asymptotic estimates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where \(\mathscr{I}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{uni}}\) is the polynomial interpolation operator using the zeros of \(H_{n_{\ell}+1}\).

Let \(n:=n_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}\) denote the number of quadrature points used in the univariate Gauss--Hermite rule \(Q_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}^{\mathrm{uni}}\), and let \(\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n}\) be the roots of the univariate Hermite polynomial \(H_{n}\) of degree \(n\).

issues.failure_explanation: The Gauss-Hermite quadrature \(Q_{\bar\ell_1}^{uni}\) uses the roots of \(H_n\), while the interpolation operator \(\mathscr{I}_{\bar\ell_1}^{uni}\) uses the roots of \(H_{n+1}\). The fact that \(\mathscr{I}\) is interpolatory does not imply \(Q(p_n)=\int \mathscr{I}(p_n)\rho\). In fact, \(Q(p_n)=0\) because \(p_n\) vanishes at the roots of \(H_n\), but \(\int \mathscr{I}(p_n)\rho\) is generally nonzero. Hence the displayed equality is false, and the intended transfer of the univariate quadrature lower bound to interpolation error is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a correct lower-bound argument for interpolation, e.g., by constructing a fooling function that vanishes at the interpolation nodes or by directly relating the interpolation error to a known univariate lower bound without the false equality.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the lower bound for sparse-grid Gauss-Hermite interpolation is invalid; the theorem's claims are unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid transfer from quadrature error to interpolation error
issues.why_classification: The central step of the proof is false, and repairing it requires a new construction or argument; the theorem's lower bound for interpolation is not established.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recall \(\Delta_{1}(1)=1\) and \(\Delta_{\ell}(1)=0\) for \(\ell\neq1\) because the Gauss--Hermite rule integrates constant functions exactly. Thus, it follows ... \(S_{\Lambda}(h_{\Lambda})=Q_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}^{\mathrm{uni}}(p_{n}),\) Hence, \(S_{\Lambda}(h_{\Lambda})=0\).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the lower bound uses the exactness of the Gauss-Hermite weights for constants to make the sparse-grid sum telescope and annihilate the fooling function. The fooling function depends only on nodes, but the fact that it is annihilated by the quadrature depends on the weights. Therefore the lower bound as proved does not apply to arbitrary modified weights, and the inference that no weight modification can improve the rate is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The lower bound is obtained by exploiting the structure of the Gauss--Hermite nodes and is independent of the quadrature weights; consequently, no modification of the weights can improve the rate \(N^{-\alpha/2}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or weaken the claim to state only that the fooling function depends on the nodes, not that the lower bound holds for arbitrary weights.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and conclusion overstate the robustness of the lower bound; the formal lower bound remains valid for the standard Gauss-Hermite rule, but the claim about arbitrary weight modifications is not established.
issues.title: Overclaim that the lower bound is independent of quadrature weights
issues.why_classification: This is a material overclaim about the scope of the result, but it does not invalidate the formal theorem for the standard rule; the repair is to weaken the prose.
